chunks: From him, from al-Baraqi, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd, from Zakariyya ibn Adam, who said:

I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) about the prey of the falcon and the hawk when they kill their prey, and a man looks at it. He said: 'Eat from it, even if it has eaten something from it as well.' I asked him three times, and each time he said the same. The reason for interpreting these narrations is that we should attribute them to taqiyya (dissimulation), which we have previously mentioned, because the rulers of the time considered it permissible, and their jurists issued fatwas regarding its permissibility. Thus, the narrations came in agreement with them, as did other narrations of a similar nature, and that which indicates this...
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat meat from game killed by a predator that has already eaten some of it?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Rida (AS) confirms the permissibility of consuming game killed by birds of prey, even if they have already eaten part of it. The narrator, Zakariyya ibn Adam, recounts asking the Imam three times to clarify whether this was a definitive ruling or an instance of *taqiyya* (dissimulation) to align with the prevailing practices of the Umayyad and Abbasid rulers and their jurists. This highlights the dynamic interplay between fixed religious law and political context in Shia jurisprudence.
